title: Shin Yami no Koe: Kaidan
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: A one-volume anthology of Junji Ito horror stories: two stories about Soichi, a curse-obsessed boy who spits nails, including one where his family adopts a stray cat; two villages that face each other with mirrors; a driver who finds a bloodied girl on a mountain road; a husband obsessed with an inherited book collection; and a song that will not leave someone's head (AniList; MU). In English these stories were collected in Viz's omnibus Smashed (MU).
life_message: No clear life message; guilt, obsession and grief turn into literal horrors.

content.note: Blood, splatter and cannibalism listed (MU Blood and Gore, Splatter, Cannibalism; AniList Body Horror); ANN reviewers note 'disturbing imagery'.
Body horror and haunted locations (AniList Body Horror rank 100; MU Haunted Location); reviewers say the tone is 'a little cold'.
A married couple in one story (blurb); nothing else noted.
Guilt-driven psychological tales and obsession (ANN review); stuck-song story (blurb).
Soichi's spitting nails and cursing people (MU blurb).

dominant: Folk curses and absurd horror; guilt and obsession

frames.aligns: Guilt has consequences in several tales.
frames.concerns: Soichi's cursing played for dark fun; gore and cannibalism.

frames.aligns: Shows passions (obsession over books) consuming people.
Little to affirm beyond warning tales.
Obsession and enmity shown as destructive.

frames.concerns: Cursing child, ghosts and haunted houses.

frames.aligns: Common-grace craft of a horror master.
Village enmity in the mirrors tale as a warning.
Enmity between villages leads to ruin.
Family heirlooms valued in one tale.

frames.concerns: Ghosts of the dead and curses as real.

frames.aligns: Village and mountain spirits in Japanese folklore.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Village feud expressed through mirrors, not courts (blurb).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Family heirloom library; Tsujii family stories (blurb).

folkways.japan: Draws on Japanese folk horror (village feuds, curses, mountain roads) as atmosphere, not message.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewers describe guilt-driven tales with a 'blithe tone'; no moralizing noted.
delivery.note: Horror vignettes with no stated thesis.

winners_losers: Most protagonists are victims of their own obsessions or curses; Soichi's mischief is played partly for dark comedy.
to_verify: AniList id is the 7-chapter Japanese volume; English readers find these stories in Viz's Smashed omnibus, whose reviews use different story titles ('Library Vision') and cover more stories.
